title: Goalkeeper apologises for punching opponent during La Liga 2 game: ‘I crossed the line’
content:
Real Zaragoza goalkeeper Esteban Andrada has apologised after striking an opponent in chaotic scenes during a Spanish second-tier match against rivals Huesca.

The clubs, who contest the Aragonese derby, also condemned the incident after the game.

In second-half stoppage time of Huesca’s 1-0 home victory, Andrada, 35, went over to speak to match official Damaso Arcediano Monescillo on the touchline, where he was confronted by Huesca captain Jorge Pulido. Andrada then pushed Pulido and received a second yellow card.

Immediately after being sent off, Andrada rushed towards Pulido and punched him, sparking a mass altercation between the players. Huesca goalkeeper Dani Jimenez received a straight red card after appearing to strike Andrada, while Zaragoza left-back Dani Tasende was also sent off.

In a statement after the match, Zaragoza condemned the “scenes unbecoming of this sport” and said that the club would be looking into the incident and would take “appropriate disciplinary measures”.

Andrada then issued an apology via the club’s social media channels.

“I really regret what happened,” the Argentine said. “It’s not a good image for the club, for the people or for a professional like me. I really regret it. Throughout my career, I’ve only been sent off once (before) when I handled the ball outside the area and you can see from my career path that it was an extreme situation where I crossed the line and I reacted like that.

“But I really regret it and I wouldn’t do it again because I know I’m a public figure, a professional with a career of many years. I also said sorry to Jorge Pulido because we’re colleagues and it was an action from me where I disconnected in that moment. I’m here for the consequences from the league or, if they want me to go and give explanations, I’m available for that.”

Huesca also issued a statement condemning the scenes and said that they accepted Andrada’s apology.

Andrada is on loan at Zaragoza from Mexican club Monterrey and has served as the club’s first-choice goalkeeper this season, featuring 28 times in all competitions. He has been capped four times by Argentina, with each appearance coming in friendly matches in 2019.
